abTest.title: A/B test of the subject line
abTest.explain: Test a second subject line on part of your audience. After the waiting time, the rest gets the subject line with the highest click rate.

abTest.subject_b_placeholder: A second version of your subject line

abTest.rule: The test group ({{percent}}%) gets half subject line A and half subject line B. After {{hours}} h, the subject line with the highest click rate wins (on a tie the highest open rate, otherwise A) and the rest gets that subject line. Each variant needs at least 100 recipients.
abTest.confirm_title: A/B test of the subject line
abTest.confirm_flow: {{perVariant}} recipients get subject line A now and {{perVariant}} get subject line B. After {{hours}} h, the remaining {{remainder}} recipients get the subject line with the highest click rate.
abTest.confirm_limit: All {{recipients}} recipients already count toward your monthly limit now, including those waiting for the winner.
abTest.too_small: Your audience is too small for the A/B test: with {{percent}}% you need at least {{min}} recipients (100 per variant). The campaign goes to everyone with subject line A.
abTest.not_possible_multi: This campaign is in several languages, so there is no A/B test: everyone gets the subject line of their language.
abTest.report_title: A/B test of the subject line
abTest.report_winner: Subject line {{variant}} won; the rest of your audience got that subject line.
abTest.report_pending: The winner will be picked around {{time}}.
abTest.report_rule: Winner = highest click rate, on a tie highest open rate, otherwise A. Opens are an approximation: some email apps preload or block images.
abTest.skipped_too_small: Your audience was too small for the test when sending (at least 100 per variant). Everyone gets subject line A.
abTest.skipped_other: The A/B test could not run for this campaign. Everyone gets the regular subject line.
abTest.report_no_difference: No difference, A chosen: nothing in the test group was opened or clicked yet.
